sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- codemode: Run JavaScript that calls other tools

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description:
Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

Codemode: `tools.read(args)` resolves to `string | { data: string; mimeType: string; note: string; type: "image"; }`.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description:
Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

Codemode: `tools.bash(args)` resolves to `{ output, truncated, full_output_path?, exit_code, wall_time_seconds }`.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description:
Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

Codemode: `tools.edit(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description:
Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

Codemode: `tools.write(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: codemode
toolsAdded.description:
Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.
- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
- Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`

Globals:
- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.
- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.
- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.
- `models`: classifiers and image generation. Read /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/codemode.md first.

content.text:
Task B1 — implement the four sparsity methods (implementation + tests + smoke runs ONLY; do not run
the full pilot matrix yet).

Read predictions.md "Part B" (B.1–B.4). It is FROZEN: eligible tensors, fine-tuning budgets,
calibration subset, S2 group definitions and keep-count formula, S3 score, S4 block orientation,
patterns (3:4, 2:4, 1:4, 1:10) and partial-block rule, the two runtime paths. Implement it exactly;
if something is impossible, stop and report instead of changing it. uv only; CPU; frozen threads.

Preliminary fixes from my A2 review:
P1. compressed_bytes must be reserved for the compact-export artifact (Part B path 2). Put the gzip-9
    size of the dense state_dict file in its own field gzip_bytes (for every run, dense included).
    Update SCHEMA.md.
P2. pytest must never write to results/runs.jsonl. Make the results path configurable (e.g. env var
    LAB3_RESULTS_DIR) and have tests use a tmp dir. The bench rows that earlier pytest runs already
    appended stay untouched; list their run_ids in results/ANNOTATIONS.md as "generated by test suite".

Implementation (code/lab3/sparsity/ or similar):
1. Masks and surgery are SEPARATE code paths: mask-based methods (S1, S3, S4) produce per-tensor binary
   masks applied to a dense-shaped model; S2 does physical surgery producing a smaller dense model.
2. Calibration subset: create splits/fmnist_calib_idx.npy exactly per B.1 (1,024 training-split
   indices, stratified, seed 12345) once, hash it into SPLITS.sha256 (append, don't regenerate others).
3. Fine-tuning per B.1 budget, re-applying masks after every optimizer step; checkpoint = best val
   epoch within the budget (ties -> later epoch).
4. Reversible mapping: save masks (S1/S3/S4) and kept-group indices per layer (S2) so the pruned model
   can be mapped back into dense parent shapes (scatter into zeros) — include a function and test.
5. Runtime paths per B.4, benchmarked with the frozen latency protocol:
   path dense_zeros (every arm); path compact: S2 = rebuilt model; S1/S3 = weights as torch.sparse_csr
   with sparse x dense matmul (and the CSR file on disk); S4 = packed N:M file on disk (kept values +
   per-value index), runtime = probe whether any semi-structured CPU kernel exists
   (e.g. torch.sparse.to_sparse_semi_structured); if not, record runtime_status "unsupported:<reason>"
   and benchmark the dense fallback, clearly labeled. Never infer speedup from zero counts.
6. Records: each arm emits two rows, stage=post_prune and stage=post_finetune, sharing an arm_id, with
   parent_run_id = the canonical seed-0 dense training run. Add fields: method params (target, nm
   pattern, group sparsity for S2), achieved_sparsity (over eligible weights), achieved_param_sparsity
   (vs dense total params), per_layer table (name, shape, numel, nonzero, sparsity), est_macs,
   est_macs_nonzero, dense_bytes/gzip_bytes for the dense_zeros path, compressed_bytes for the compact
   path, latency and rss for BOTH paths, runtime_status per path. Failures get a row with
   status=failed and a classified reason (e.g. unsupported_backend, numerical, bug, not_applicable).
7. Save every pruned post-finetune model to checkpoints/pilot/<arm_id>.pt with its masks/indices.
8. CLI: `uv run python -m lab3 prune --model {mlp,cnn,gcn} --method {s1,s2,s3,s4} --target
   {0.25,0.5,0.75,0.9} --seed K` (S4 maps targets to the frozen patterns 3:4/2:4/1:4/1:10).

Tests (must pass, never weakened):
 a. pruned entries remain exactly zero after fine-tuning (S1, S3, S4; each architecture);
 b. S2 structured shapes consistent: rebuilt models run forward, have the predicted shapes and param
    counts for every target on all three architectures (e.g. GCN at 0.9 keeps 2 hidden features);
 c. save/reload of a pruned checkpoint reproduces logits exactly and the same val/test metrics;
 d. achieved sparsity verified tensor by tensor: S1/S3 global fraction exact to within one weight;
    S4 every complete block has exactly N nonzeros (given distinct magnitudes) and partial blocks
    follow the ceil rule;
 e. reversible mapping round-trip: mapped-back weights equal the parent on kept entries, zero
    elsewhere;
 f. S3 uses only calibration-subset inputs/training labels (assert indices ⊂ train split).

Smoke runs (real records): MLP at target 0.5 for each of S1, S2, S3, S4 (2:4), seed 0. Then STOP and
report: files changed, test output, the four smoke rows (val/test pre/post FT, achieved sparsity,
both-path bytes and latency, runtime_status), and every anomaly or limitation you found.

# Lab 3 — Predictions and Frozen Design Decisions

Each section is dated and was written **before** the runs it governs. Sections are
append-only: later corrections are added as dated amendments, never by editing a frozen
section.

---

## Part A — Dense reference models (frozen 2026-11-09, before any training)

### A.1 Frozen design

**Hardware / software.** Apple M4 Pro (12 CPU cores), 24 GB RAM, macOS. Python 3.12,
PyTorch 2.15.0, torchvision 0.29.2, torch_geometric 2.8.1, NumPy 2.5.4. Package
management with `uv` (`pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock`). **CPU only for every arm**; no MPS.

**Threads.** `torch.set_num_threads(4)` and `torch.set_num_interop_threads(1)` for all
training, evaluation, and benchmarking.

**Data splits (created once, saved to `splits/`, reused by every arm).**
- Fashion-MNIST: official 60k train / 10k test. From the 60k train set, a stratified
  5,000-image validation set (500 per class) is drawn once with split seed 12345; the
  remaining 55,000 images are the training set. The 10k official test set is the test set.
  Saved as index files plus a SHA-256 of the index arrays.
- Cora: the standard Planetoid public split (140 train / 500 val / 1000 test nodes), saved
  as node-index files with a SHA-256. The graph (2,708 nodes, 10,556 directed edges) is
  never modified by any compression arm.
- Inputs: Fashion-MNIST normalized with mean/std computed on the 55k training split only.
  Cora features row-normalized (standard GCN preprocessing).

**Architectures.**
| Model | Definition | Params (computed) |
|---|---|---|
| MLP | 784→256→128→10, ReLU, no dropout | 235,146 |
| CNN | Conv(1→16, 5×5, pad 2)→ReLU→MaxPool2 → Conv(16→32, 5×5)→ReLU→MaxPool2 → FC(800→128)→ReLU → FC(128→10) | 117,066 |
| GCN | GCNConv(1433→16)→ReLU→Dropout(0.5) → GCNConv(16→7) | 23,063 |

No BatchNorm anywhere (keeps INT8 conversion and structured surgery unambiguous).

**Training.**
- MLP and CNN: Adam, lr 1e-3, weight decay 0, batch size 128, cross-entropy, max **30
  epochs**.
- GCN: Adam, lr 0.01, weight decay 5e-4, full-batch, cross-entropy on the 140 train nodes,
  max **300 epochs**.

**Early stopping / checkpoint selection (validation only).** After each epoch, evaluate
validation accuracy. Keep the checkpoint with the highest validation accuracy; ties go to
the lower validation loss, then to the earlier epoch. Stop when validation accuracy has not
improved for **5 epochs** (MLP, CNN) or **50 epochs** (GCN), or at the max epoch count. The
test set is evaluated only on the selected checkpoint and never feeds back into any choice.

**Seeds.** Each run sets Python `random`, NumPy, and PyTorch seeds to the run seed and logs
it.
- Pilot seed: **0**. Produces the canonical dense checkpoint per architecture. Every
  compression arm starts from it, and the full Part B pilot matrix uses it.
- Confirmatory seeds: **1, 2, 3**. Used (a) to train three replica dense baselines per
  architecture, which report seed variance only and are never used as compression parents,
  and (b) in Part B to repeat the selected operating points. There the seed controls
  fine-tuning shuffle order and dropout, and the parent is always the canonical seed-0
  checkpoint.
- The split seed 12345 is separate from these and is never changed.

**Sanity targets (test accuracy).** MLP ≥ 82%, CNN ≥ 87%, GCN ≥ 65%. A miss is diagnosed,
and the cause is recorded. The target is not lowered.

**Latency protocol.** `torch.inference_mode()`, model in `eval()`. 20 warm-up and 200
timed iterations, timed with `time.perf_counter_ns`. Report the median and IQR. Batch sizes
are **1** and **256** for Fashion-MNIST, and one full-graph forward pass for Cora. Peak RSS
is measured in a fresh subprocess per benchmark.

**Stopping rule for agent work.** If a baseline misses its target after one diagnosed fix,
or any required test fails twice after a fix, work stops and the issue is reviewed before
continuing. Tests are never weakened to pass.

### A.2 Predictions

**Parameter count: MLP (235k) > CNN (117k) > GCN (23k).**
*Mechanism:* the MLP's first layer alone (784×256 ≈ 201k) dominates its count. The CNN
shares 5×5 kernels across positions, so its convolutions are tiny (≈13k), and most of its
parameters sit in FC(800→128) (≈103k). The GCN has a 16-wide hidden layer, so nearly all
of its parameters are the 1433×16 input projection.

**Dense checkpoint size: MLP (~0.94 MB) > CNN (~0.47 MB) > GCN (~0.09 MB).**
*Mechanism:* FP32 state dicts are about 4 bytes × params, plus a few KB of pickle/zip
overhead. The overhead is proportionally largest for the GCN, so its ratio to the others
will be slightly above the raw parameter ratio. The Cora graph is data, not checkpoint.

**Training time to the selected checkpoint: CNN > MLP > GCN.**
*Mechanism:* per image, the CNN does about 1.7M MACs (conv2 alone is about 1.28M), against
0.235M for the MLP. That is about 7× more compute over the same 55k images per epoch,
partly offset by better-optimized conv kernels. The GCN trains full-batch on 2,708 nodes.
Each epoch is one sparse aggregation plus a 2708×1433×16 projection, so 300 epochs should
take seconds, against minutes for the image models.

**Sensitivity to compression (most to least): GCN > CNN > MLP.**
*Mechanism:*
- *GCN:* it has a 16-dimensional bottleneck and only 140 labelled nodes for fine-tuning.
  Every remaining weight carries a large share of the representation, and recovery data is
  scarce. Most of its input-projection weights belong to rare bag-of-words features, so
  moderate unstructured sparsity should be tolerated. At high sparsity, and for structured
  removal of hidden features, I expect the sharpest collapse.
- *CNN:* convolution weights are reused at every spatial position, so pruning one conv
  weight perturbs many activations. Global magnitude pruning should mostly remove FC
  weights, which buffers it, but structured channel pruning of a 16/32-channel network
  should hurt.
- *MLP:* it is heavily over-parameterized for Fashion-MNIST. Many first-layer weights
  attach to border pixels with near-constant input, so they carry little signal and should
  prune almost for free up to high sparsity.
- *Precision:* I predict INT8 costs every model < 0.5 pp of accuracy. Simulated INT4 should
  hurt the GCN and CNN more than the MLP, for the same bottleneck and weight-reuse reasons.

**Expected baseline test accuracy:** MLP about 88–89%, CNN about 90–91%, GCN about 80–81%.

---

## Part B — Four forms of sparsity (frozen 2026-11-09, before any pruning run)

### B.1 Common protocol (all four methods)

- **Parent:** every arm starts from the canonical seed-0 dense checkpoint of its
  architecture (`checkpoints/dense/<arch>_seed0.pt`).
- **One-shot pruning,** followed by a fixed fine-tuning budget. There is no iterative
  pruning.
- **Eligible tensors:** the weight matrix/kernel of every Linear, Conv2d, and GCNConv layer,
  including the final classifier. Biases are never pruned, and there are no normalization
  layers.
- **Fine-tuning budget (identical for every method within an architecture):**
  - MLP/CNN: 3 epochs, Adam lr 5e-4, batch 128, frozen 55k training split.
  - GCN: 50 epochs, Adam lr 0.005, weight decay 5e-4, dropout 0.5, 140 training nodes.
  - The fine-tuning checkpoint is the epoch with the best validation accuracy inside that
    budget. Ties go to the later epoch, which is the more-trained model.
- **Masks:** for S1/S3/S4 a binary mask is re-applied after every optimizer step, so pruned
  entries stay exactly zero. Adam state for masked entries is irrelevant because the mask
  is applied to the weights.
- **Measurement stages:** every arm is measured twice: immediately after pruning, before
  any update (`stage=post_prune`), and after fine-tuning (`stage=post_finetune`). Both rows
  carry val/test accuracy, per-layer sparsity, bytes, MACs, latency, and memory.
- **Pilot:** seed 0 for the full 3 × 4 × 4 matrix. In fine-tuning, the seed controls data
  order and dropout.
- **Calibration subset (S3 now, reused in Part C):**
  - Fashion-MNIST: 1,024 images from the **training** split, stratified 102–103 per class,
    drawn once with seed 12345 and saved to `splits/fmnist_calib_idx.npy`. The labels are
    training labels.
  - Cora: the 140 training nodes on the full graph.
  - No validation or test labels are ever used for calibration.

### B.2 Method specifications

**S1 Global unstructured magnitude.** Pool all eligible weights across layers, then zero
the fraction *s* with the smallest |w|. Targets: 25/50/75/90%. Achieved sparsity is
reported globally and per tensor.

**S2 Structured group pruning (L1).** Groups and their L1 norms:
- MLP: hidden units of both hidden layers. The norm is the unit's incoming weight row.
- CNN: output channels of conv1 and conv2 (L1 of each filter) and FC1 hidden units.
  Removing conv2 channels also removes the matching FC1 input columns.
- GCN: the 16 hidden features. The norm is the incoming weight column of layer 1.

Ranking is **layer-wise**: each prunable layer removes the same fraction, keeping
k = max(1, round((1 − s)·n)) groups. The classifier output and the input dimension are
never pruned. The model is **physically rebuilt** as a smaller dense model by copying the
surviving rows/columns/bias entries. The target is the fraction of groups removed, and the
achieved value is reported as both group sparsity and parameter sparsity relative to the
dense model. These differ. For example, at s = 90%, GCN keeps round(1.6) = 2 features, so
87.5% of groups are removed.

**S3 First-order saliency (unstructured, global; this choice is fixed).** The score is
|w ⊙ ∂L/∂w|, where L is the mean cross-entropy over the whole calibration subset (one
gradient computed on the dense parent in eval mode, so no dropout). Pool all eligible
weights across layers and zero the lowest-scoring fraction *s*.

**S4 N:M semi-structured.**
- Blocks are M consecutive weights along each row's **reduction (input) dimension**. Conv
  kernels are flattened to [out, in·k·k]. In each block, keep the N largest |w|.
- If the row length is not divisible by M, the final partial block of length r keeps
  ⌈N·r/M⌉ weights.
- **Patterns, chosen before running:** 3:4 (25%), 2:4 (50%), 1:4 (75%), and 1:10 (90%,
  following the instructor's guidance). Every pilot cell is filled by a real run.
- Partial blocks make achieved sparsity slightly below the nominal value for rows with
  remainders: conv1 rows have 25 weights, and GCN layer 1 rows have 1,433. Achieved
  sparsity is reported.
- No cell is filled by copying another run.

### B.3 Confirmatory point selection rule (validation only; fixed before any test result is seen)

For each architecture × method, take the pilot (seed 0) post-fine-tune rows:

1. **Eligible levels:** post-fine-tune validation accuracy ≥ dense seed-0 validation
   accuracy − τ. τ = 1.0 pp for MLP and CNN. τ = 2.0 pp for GCN, whose 500-node validation
   set gives one node = 0.2 pp and a binomial SE of ~1.8 pp.
2. **Choose** the eligible level with the **highest target sparsity**.
3. **Fallback:** if no level is eligible, choose the level with the highest post-fine-tune
   validation accuracy. Ties go to the lower sparsity.
4. **Rerun** the chosen point with seeds 1, 2, 3, using the same parent and budget.

Test accuracy is logged but never read by this rule.

### B.4 Two runtime paths

- **Path 1:** dense PyTorch modules holding zero-valued weights. Run this for every arm.
- **Path 2: genuinely compact export.**
  - S2: the physically rebuilt dense model.
  - S1/S3: `torch.sparse_csr` weights executed with sparse matmul (sparse × dense), plus
    a CSR file on disk.
  - S4: a packed N:M file (kept values + a small index per kept value) for size.
- If the CPU backend has no semi-structured kernel, S4 runtime is recorded as unsupported
  or dense-fallback. It is never inferred from the zero count.

### B.5 Predictions (per method)

**S1 global magnitude.**
- *(i) Largest loss at 75%:* **GCN**, about −1 pp after fine-tuning. It has the smallest
  network and the least labelled data for recovery. Before fine-tuning I expect MLP ≈ −1,
  CNN ≈ −2, and GCN ≈ −3 pp.
- *(ii) Recovery:* fine-tuning recovers almost all loss up to 75%. At 90% it recovers most,
  leaving MLP/CNN about 1–2 pp and GCN about 3–5 pp below dense.
- *(iii) Size and runtime:*
  - The dense-path file size and latency will **not** change, because zeros are stored and
    multiplied as FP32. Gzip will shrink the file roughly with sparsity.
  - CSR export becomes smaller than dense only above roughly 60–67% sparsity, since each
    nonzero costs 4 B of value plus an 8 B int64 column index.
  - Sparse matmul will be **slower** than dense at every level for these small layers,
    including 90%.

**S2 structured.**
- *(i) Largest loss at 75%:* **CNN before fine-tuning.** It drops to 4 and 8 channels and
  each removed channel loses a whole feature map, so I expect a drop of tens of pp.
  **GCN after fine-tuning:** 4 hidden features for 7 classes is a bottleneck narrower than
  the class count, and I expect −5 to −10 pp.
- *(ii) Recovery:* fine-tuning recovers most of the loss for MLP/CNN, leaving them 1–3 pp
  below dense at 75%. It recovers less for GCN.
- *(iii) Size and runtime:* the only method with **real** dense-path reductions.
  - File size shrinks roughly with parameters.
  - At batch 256, MLP/CNN latency falls roughly with MACs.
  - At batch 1, latency is dominated by framework overhead (~10 µs), so the speedup is
    small.
  - GCN latency falls modestly because the X·W projection shrinks, while aggregation and
    overhead remain.

**S3 saliency (unstructured).**
- *(i) Largest loss at 75%:* **GCN**. Its post-prune accuracy should be slightly better than
  S1 at 50–75% because the score accounts for the gradient. At 90%, a gradient taken at a
  near-converged dense point is noisy, so I expect it to be no better than S1.
- *(ii) Recovery:* similar to S1.
- *(iii) Size and runtime:* same as S1, since it produces the same unstructured format.

**S4 N:M.**
- *(i) Largest loss at 75% (1:4):* **CNN** before fine-tuning. The local per-block
  constraint is harsher than global ranking, and conv1 has only 25 weights per filter.
  After fine-tuning, the GCN loses the most.
- *(ii) Recovery:* 3:4 and 2:4 recover to within about 0.5 pp. 1:4 and 1:10 lose more than
  S1 at the same sparsity, because the pattern can't concentrate surviving weights in the
  important rows.
- *(iii) Size and runtime:*
  - I predict **no runtime gain** on this laptop, because PyTorch has no semi-structured
    sparse CPU kernel on ARM. Expect a dense fallback.
  - The packed N:M file will be smaller than dense at 2:4 and sparser levels.
  - Dense-path file size is unchanged.

**Cross-method expectation:** for deployment on this laptop, only S2 will improve both size
and measured latency. S1/S3/S4 will mainly show that more zeros ≠ faster.

"""CLI for the Lab 3 dense-reference package.

Usage: uv run python -m lab3 <cmd> --model {mlp,cnn,gcn} ...
Commands: make-splits, train, eval, bench.
Configs live in configs/<model>.yaml and hold the frozen hyperparameters.
CLI flags may override config values for tests only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import yaml
import torch

from .util import (
    CONFIGS_DIR,
    DATA_DIR,
    SPLIT_SEED,
    SPLITS_DIR,
    compute_splits_hash,
    set_threads,
)


def load_config(architecture: str) -> dict:
    path = CONFIGS_DIR / f"{architecture}.yaml"
    if not path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"missing config {path}")
    with open(path) as f:
        return yaml.safe_load(f)


def _cora_masks() -> tuple:
    from torch_geometric.datasets import Planetoid
    from .util import DATA_DIR as _D
    ds = Planetoid(root=str(_D / "Planetoid"), name="Cora")
    g = ds[0]
    return g.train_mask, g.val_mask, g.test_mask


def make_splits_impl() -> None:
    set_threads()
    import lab3.util as U
    existing = [p for p in U.SPLIT_FILES["fmnist"] + U.SPLIT_FILES["cora"] + [U.SPLITS_SHA]]
    if any(p.exists() for p in existing):
        raise FileExistsError("splits already exist; refusing to regenerate. "
                              "Delete splits/ manually only if you intend to reset all arms.")
    U.SPLITS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    np.random.seed(SPLIT_SEED)

    from .data import _fmnist_dataset
    train_ds = _fmnist_dataset("train")
    labels = np.asarray(train_ds.targets)
    assert labels.shape[0] == 60000
    val_idx = []
    for cls in range(10):
        pool = np.flatnonzero(labels == cls)
        val_idx.append(np.random.permutation(pool)[:500])
    val_idx = np.sort(np.concatenate(val_idx))
    train_idx = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(60000), val_idx, assume_unique=True)
    test_idx = np.arange(10000)
    assert train_idx.shape[0] == 55000 and val_idx.shape[0] == 5000

    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_train_idx.npy", train_idx.astype(np.int64))
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_val_idx.npy", val_idx.astype(np.int64))
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_test_idx.npy", test_idx.astype(np.int64))

    tr_m, va_m, te_m = _cora_masks()
    cora_tr = np.flatnonzero(tr_m.numpy())
    cora_va = np.flatnonzero(va_m.numpy())
    cora_te = np.flatnonzero(te_m.numpy())
    assert cora_tr.shape[0] == 140 and cora_va.shape[0] == 500 and cora_te.shape[0] == 1000
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "cora_train_idx.npy", cora_tr.astype(np.int64))
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "cora_val_idx.npy", cora_va.astype(np.int64))
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "cora_test_idx.npy", cora_te.astype(np.int64))

    U.SPLITS_SHA.write_text(compute_splits_hash() + "  splits/*.npy (fixed order, see compute_splits_hash)\n")
    print(f"splits written to {U.SPLITS_DIR}; hash={compute_splits_hash()}")


def _apply_overrides(cfg: dict, args) -> dict:
    """CLI flags override frozen config values (for tests only)."""
    for flag, key in (("--lr", "lr"), ("--weight-decay", "weight_decay"),
                      ("--batch-size", "batch_size"), ("--epochs", "max_epochs"),
                      ("--patience", "patience")):
        val = getattr(args, flag.replace("-", "_"), None)
        if val is not None:
            cfg[key] = val
    return cfg


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="lab3")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    p = sub.add_parser("make-splits")
    p.set_defaults(fn=make_splits_impl)

    for name, help_ in (("train", "train a dense model"),
                        ("eval", "evaluate a saved checkpoint"),
                        ("bench", "benchmark a saved checkpoint")):
        p = sub.add_parser(name, help=help_)
        p.add_argument("--model", required=True, choices=["mlp", "cnn", "gcn"])
        p.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
        p.add_argument("--run-id", default=None)
        # overrides (tests only)
        p.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=None)
        p.add_argument("--weight-decay", type=float, default=None)
        p.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=None)
        p.add_argument("--epochs", type=int, default=None)
        p.add_argument("--patience", type=int, default=None)

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    set_threads()

    if args.cmd == "make-splits":
        args.fn()
        return 0

    cfg = load_config(args.model)
    cfg = _apply_overrides(cfg, args)

    if args.cmd == "train":
        from .training import train
        rec = train(args.model, cfg, seed=args.seed, run_id=args.run_id)
        print(f"run_id={rec['run_id']} best_epoch={rec['best_epoch']} "
              f"val_acc={rec['val_acc']:.4f} test_acc={rec['test_acc']:.4f} "
              f"epochs={rec['train_epochs']} wall={rec['wall_time_s']}s")
    elif args.cmd == "eval":
        from .evaln import eval as do_eval
        rec = do_eval(args.model, seed=args.seed)
        print(f"run_id={rec['run_id']} val_acc={rec['val_acc']:.4f} test_acc={rec['test_acc']:.4f}")
    elif args.cmd == "bench":
        from .bench import bench
        rec = bench(args.model, seed=args.seed)
        lat = rec["latency"]
        print(f"run_id={rec['run_id']} latency={lat} peak_rss={rec['peak_rss_bytes']}B")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Shared utilities: frozen environment setup, splits, run logging, code hash."""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch

# Repo root (project root): <root>/code/lab3/util.py -> parents[2]
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
DATA_DIR = ROOT / "data"
SPLITS_DIR = ROOT / "splits"
CHECKPOINTS_DIR = ROOT / "checkpoints" / "dense"
RESULTS_DIR = ROOT / "results"
CURVES_DIR = RESULTS_DIR / "curves"
RUNS_JSONL = RESULTS_DIR / "runs.jsonl"
BENCH_DIR = RESULTS_DIR / "bench"
FIGURES_DIR = ROOT / "figures"
CONFIGS_DIR = ROOT / "configs"

SPLIT_SEED = 12345
SPLIT_FILES = {
    "fmnist": [
        SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_train_idx.npy",
        SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_val_idx.npy",
        SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_test_idx.npy",
    ],
    "cora": [
        SPLITS_DIR / "cora_train_idx.npy",
        SPLITS_DIR / "cora_val_idx.npy",
        SPLITS_DIR / "cora_test_idx.npy",
    ],
}
SPLITS_SHA = SPLITS_DIR / "SPLITS.sha256"


def set_threads() -> None:
    """Frozen thread protocol: 4 intra-op threads, 1 inter-op thread."""
    torch.set_num_threads(4)
    try:
        torch.set_num_interop_threads(1)
    except RuntimeError:
        # interop thread count can only be set before any parallel region starts
        pass


def set_seed(seed: int) -> None:
    """Frozen seed protocol: Python random, NumPy, and PyTorch."""
    random.seed(seed)
    np.random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)


def _sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


def compute_splits_hash() -> str:
    """SHA-256 over the six split index files (fixed order, name + array bytes)."""
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    for key in ("fmnist", "cora"):
        for path in SPLIT_FILES[key]:
            h.update(path.name.encode("utf-8"))
            h.update(_sha256_file(path).encode("ascii"))
    return h.hexdigest()


def verify_splits() -> None:
    """Load all split files and verify SPLITS.sha256; never regenerates."""
    if not SPLITS_SHA.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"{SPLITS_SHA} not found. Run `uv run python -m lab3 make-splits` first. "
            "Splits are never regenerated automatically."
        )
    for key in SPLIT_FILES:
        for path in SPLIT_FILES[key]:
            if not path.exists():
                raise FileNotFoundError(f"missing split file {path}; run make-splits first")
    recorded = SPLITS_SHA.read_text().strip().split()[0]
    actual = compute_splits_hash()
    if actual != recorded:
        raise ValueError(
            f"split hash mismatch: recorded {recorded} != actual {actual}. "
            "Refusing to continue; run make-splits only if you intentionally reset splits."
        )


def load_indices(name: str) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    verify_splits()
    out = {}
    files = {"train": SPLIT_FILES[name][0], "val": SPLIT_FILES[name][1], "test": SPLIT_FILES[name][2]}
    for k, p in files.items():
        out[k] = np.load(p)
    return out


def code_hash() -> str:
    """SHA-256 over all files under code/ (git-free: pure file-content hash)."""
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    code_dir = ROOT / "code"
    for path in sorted(code_dir.rglob("*")):
        if path.is_file():
            h.update(str(path.relative_to(code_dir)).encode("utf-8"))
            h.update(path.read_bytes())
    return h.hexdigest()


def _ensure_dirs() -> None:
    for d in (DATA_DIR, SPLITS_DIR, CHECKPOINTS_DIR, RESULTS_DIR, CURVES_DIR,
              FIGURES_DIR, BENCH_DIR):
        d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)


def new_run_id(architecture: str, method: str = "dense") -> str:
    ts = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%fZ")
    return f"{architecture}-{method}-{ts}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}"


def write_run_record(rec: dict) -> None:
    """Append one JSON line to results/runs.jsonl. Never rewrites or deletes."""
    _ensure_dirs()
    with open(RUNS_JSONL, "a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(rec, default=str) + "\n")
        f.flush()
        os.fsync(f.fileno())


def prior_bench_run_ids(architecture: str, seed: int = 0) -> list[str]:
    """run_ids of all earlier successful `bench` records for this (arch, seed), in
    file order. Used to fill `supersedes` on a corrected re-bench. The log is
    append-only: earlier lines are never edited or deleted."""
    out = []
    if not RUNS_JSONL.exists():
        return out
    with open(RUNS_JSONL) as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            try:
                r = json.loads(line)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                continue
            if (r.get("command") == "bench" and r.get("status") == "ok"
                    and r.get("architecture") == architecture and r.get("seed") == seed):
                out.append(r["run_id"])
    return out


def versions() -> dict:
    import platform

    return {
        "python": platform.python_version(),
        "torch": torch.__version__,
        "numpy": np.__version__,
        "platform": platform.platform(),
    }


def base_record(architecture: str, command: str) -> dict:
    return {
        "run_id": new_run_id(architecture),
        "status": "ok",
        "reason": None,
        "part": "A",
        "architecture": architecture,
        "method": "dense",
        "target_sparsity": 0.0,
        "achieved_sparsity": 0.0,
        "stored_precision": "fp32",
        "compute_precision": "fp32",
        "accumulator_precision": "fp32",
        "seed": None,
        "train_epochs": None,
        "finetune_epochs": 0,
        "best_epoch": None,
        "val_acc": None,
        "val_loss": None,
        "test_acc": None,
        "total_params": None,
        "nonzero_params": None,
        "dense_bytes": None,
        "raw_tensor_bytes": None,
        "compressed_bytes": None,
        "est_macs": None,
        "est_macs_nonzero": None,
        "est_macs_sparse_input": None,
        "gcn_norm_macs": None,
        "peak_rss_bytes": None,
        "rss_before_model_bytes": None,
        "model_rss_delta_bytes": None,
        "latency": {},
        "parent_run_id": None,
        "supersedes": [],
        "wall_time_s": None,
        "code_hash": code_hash(),
        "versions": versions(),
        "timestamp": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "command": command,
    }


def finalize_record(rec: dict, *, status: str | None = None, reason: str | None = None) -> dict:
    if status is not None:
        rec["status"] = status
        rec["reason"] = reason
    return rec


def run_wall_timer(rec: dict, t0: float) -> dict:
    rec["wall_time_s"] = round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 3)
    return rec

"""Data loading: Fashion-MNIST and Cora (Planetoid public split)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import torch
from torchvision import datasets as tv_datasets


def _fmnist_dataset(mode: str) -> tv_datasets.FashionMNIST:
    """mode in {'train','test'}: official 60k/10k sets, raw uint8 pixels."""
    from .util import DATA_DIR

    return tv_datasets.FashionMNIST(
        root=str(DATA_DIR), train=(mode == "train"), download=True
    )


def _images(ds: tv_datasets.FashionMNIST, idx: np.ndarray) -> torch.Tensor:
    """(N,1,28,28) float32 tensor for the given indices (raw 0..255)."""
    out = torch.empty((len(idx), 1, 28, 28), dtype=torch.float32)
    for row, i in enumerate(idx):
        out[row] = torch.from_numpy(np.asarray(ds[int(i)][0])).view(1, 28, 28)
    return out


def fmnist_split_tensors():
    """Return (train_x, train_y, val_x, val_y, test_x, test_y, mean, std) as float32
    tensors. Normalization mean/std computed on the 55k training split only (frozen).
    Indices come from the verified split files."""
    from .util import load_indices, set_threads

    set_threads()
    idx = load_indices("fmnist")
    train_ds = _fmnist_dataset("train")
    test_ds = _fmnist_dataset("test")
    tr_x = _images(train_ds, idx["train"])
    tr_y = torch.tensor([train_ds.targets[int(i)] for i in idx["train"]], dtype=torch.long)
    va_x = _images(train_ds, idx["val"])
    va_y = torch.tensor([train_ds.targets[int(i)] for i in idx["val"]], dtype=torch.long)
    te_x = _images(test_ds, idx["test"])
    te_y = torch.tensor([test_ds.targets[int(i)] for i in idx["test"]], dtype=torch.long)
    # Frozen: mean/std on the 55k training split only
    mean = tr_x.mean(dim=(0, 2, 3), keepdim=True)
    std = tr_x.std(dim=(0, 2, 3), keepdim=True)
    tr_x = (tr_x - mean) / std
    va_x = (va_x - mean) / std
    te_x = (te_x - mean) / std
    return tr_x, tr_y, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y, mean, std


def load_cora():
    """Load Cora (Planetoid public split) and apply the frozen preprocessing:
    row-normalized features (x / (rowsum + 1e-12)). Returns a Data object with
    float32 features and the verified node index tensors lm_train/lm_val/lm_test."""
    from torch_geometric.datasets import Planetoid

    from .util import DATA_DIR, load_indices, set_threads

    set_threads()
    dataset = Planetoid(root=str(DATA_DIR / "Planetoid"), name="Cora")
    data = dataset[0]

    # Frozen: Cora features row-normalized (standard GCN preprocessing).
    x = data.x
    row_sum = x.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
    data.x = (x / (row_sum + 1e-12)).to(torch.float32)

    idx = load_indices("cora")
    data.lm_train = torch.tensor(idx["train"], dtype=torch.long)
    data.lm_val = torch.tensor(idx["val"], dtype=torch.long)
    data.lm_test = torch.tensor(idx["test"], dtype=torch.long)
    return data

"""Frozen training loop with validation-selected checkpointing (Part A.1)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import time

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, TensorDataset

from .data import fmnist_split_tensors, load_cora
from .models import build_model, count_params, dense_bytes
from .util import (
    CHECKPOINTS_DIR,
    CURVES_DIR,
    RESULTS_DIR,
    base_record,
    new_run_id,
    run_wall_timer,
    set_seed,
    set_threads,
    write_run_record,
)


def _eval_fmnist(model, x, y, batch_size=1024) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Validation/test evaluation on Fashion-MNIST. Eval mode only; no weight updates."""
    model.eval()
    with torch.inference_mode():
        n = len(y)
        correct = 0
        loss_sum = 0.0
        for i in range(0, n, batch_size):
            xb, yb = x[i:i + batch_size], y[i:i + batch_size]
            out = model(xb)
            loss_sum += float(nn.functional.cross_entropy(out, yb, reduction="sum").item())
            correct += int((out.argmax(dim=1) == yb).sum().item())
    return correct / n, loss_sum / n


def _eval_cora(model, data, mask) -> tuple[float, float]:
    model.eval()
    with torch.inference_mode():
        out = model(data.x, data.edge_index)
        out = out[mask]
        y = data.y[mask]
        loss = float(nn.functional.cross_entropy(out, y).item())
        acc = float((out.argmax(dim=1) == y).float().mean().item())
    return acc, loss


def _checkpoint_path(architecture: str, seed: int):
    return CHECKPOINTS_DIR / f"{architecture}_seed{seed}.pt"


def _is_best(cand: tuple, best: tuple | None) -> bool:
    """cand=(val_acc, val_loss, epoch). Higher acc wins; tie -> lower loss; tie -> earlier epoch."""
    if best is None:
        return True
    ca, cl, ce = cand
    ba, bl, be = best
    if ca > ba:
        return True
    if ca == ba and cl < bl:
        return True
    if ca == ba and cl == bl and ce < be:
        return True
    return False


def _save_curve(run_id: str, rows: list[dict]) -> None:
    CURVES_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = CURVES_DIR / f"{run_id}.csv"
    with open(path, "w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=rows[0].keys())
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)


def train(architecture: str, cfg: dict, seed: int, run_id: str | None = None) -> dict:
    """Frozen training protocol. Returns the run record (also appended to runs.jsonl)."""
    set_threads()
    set_seed(seed)
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    rec = base_record(architecture, command="train")
    rec["run_id"] = run_id or new_run_id(architecture)
    rec["seed"] = seed
    curve_rows: list[dict] = []

    try:
        model = build_model(architecture)
        rec["total_params"] = count_params(model)
        rec["nonzero_params"] = count_params(model)
        rec["dense_bytes"] = dense_bytes(model)

        if architecture == "gcn":
            data = load_cora()
            train_idx, val_idx, test_idx = data.lm_train, data.lm_val, data.lm_test
            max_epochs = int(cfg["max_epochs"])
            patience = int(cfg["patience"])
            opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=float(cfg["lr"]),
                                   weight_decay=float(cfg["weight_decay"]))

            best: tuple | None = None
            best_state: dict | None = None
            epochs_no_improve = 0
            epochs_trained = 0
            for epoch in range(1, max_epochs + 1):
                model.train()
                opt.zero_grad()
                out = model(data.x, data.edge_index)
                loss = nn.functional.cross_entropy(out[train_idx], data.y[train_idx])
                loss.backward()
                opt.step()
                epochs_trained = epoch

                va_acc, va_loss = _eval_cora(model, data, val_idx)
                curve_rows.append({"epoch": epoch, "train_loss": float(loss.item()),
                                   "val_acc": va_acc, "val_loss": va_loss})
                if _is_best((va_acc, va_loss, epoch), best):
                    best = (va_acc, va_loss, epoch)
                    best_state = {k: v.detach().clone() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()}
                    epochs_no_improve = 0
                else:
                    epochs_no_improve += 1
                if epochs_no_improve >= patience:
                    break

            rec["train_epochs"] = epochs_trained
            rec["best_epoch"] = best[2]
            rec["val_acc"] = best[0]
            rec["val_loss"] = best[1]
            # Test set evaluated only on the selected checkpoint
            model.load_state_dict(best_state)
            te_acc, _ = _eval_cora(model, data, test_idx)
            rec["test_acc"] = te_acc
            _save_checkpoint(architecture, seed, model, rec, cfg)
        else:
            tr_x, tr_y, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y, mean, std = fmnist_split_tensors()
            batch_size = int(cfg["batch_size"])
            max_epochs = int(cfg["max_epochs"])
            patience = int(cfg["patience"])
            opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=float(cfg["lr"]),
                                   weight_decay=float(cfg["weight_decay"]))
            loader = DataLoader(TensorDataset(tr_x, tr_y), batch_size=batch_size,
                                shuffle=True, drop_last=False)

            best = None
            best_state = None
            epochs_no_improve = 0
            epochs_trained = 0
            for epoch in range(1, max_epochs + 1):
                model.train()
                correct = 0
                loss_sum = 0.0
                n = 0
                for xb, yb in loader:
                    opt.zero_grad()
                    out = model(xb)
                    loss = nn.functional.cross_entropy(out, yb)
                    loss.backward()
                    opt.step()
                    loss_sum += float(loss.item()) * len(yb)
                    correct += int((out.argmax(dim=1) == yb).sum().item())
                    n += len(yb)
                epochs_trained = epoch
                va_acc, va_loss = _eval_fmnist(model, va_x, va_y)
                curve_rows.append({"epoch": epoch, "train_loss": loss_sum / n,
                                   "train_acc": correct / n,
                                   "val_acc": va_acc, "val_loss": va_loss})
                if _is_best((va_acc, va_loss, epoch), best):
                    best = (va_acc, va_loss, epoch)
                    best_state = {k: v.detach().clone() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()}
                    epochs_no_improve = 0
                else:
                    epochs_no_improve += 1
                if epochs_no_improve >= patience:
                    break

            rec["train_epochs"] = epochs_trained
            rec["best_epoch"] = best[2]
            rec["val_acc"] = best[0]
            rec["val_loss"] = best[1]
            model.load_state_dict(best_state)
            te_acc, _ = _eval_fmnist(model, te_x, te_y)
            rec["test_acc"] = te_acc
            _save_checkpoint(architecture, seed, model, rec, cfg)

        _save_curve(rec["run_id"], curve_rows)
        rec = run_wall_timer(rec, t0)
        write_run_record(rec)
        return rec

    except Exception as e:  # record crashes; never leave runs.jsonl silent
        rec = run_wall_timer(rec, t0)
        rec["status"] = "failed"
        rec["reason"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        try:
            if curve_rows:
                _save_curve(rec["run_id"], curve_rows)
        except Exception:
            pass
        write_run_record(rec)
        raise


def _save_checkpoint(architecture: str, seed: int, model, rec: dict, cfg: dict) -> None:
    CHECKPOINTS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    model.eval()
    torch.save({
        "state_dict": {k: v.detach().clone() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()},
        "metadata": {
            "architecture": architecture,
            "seed": seed,
            "best_epoch": rec["best_epoch"],
            "train_epochs": rec["train_epochs"],
            "val_acc": rec["val_acc"],
            "val_loss": rec["val_loss"],
            "test_acc": rec["test_acc"],
            "config": cfg,
            "run_id": rec["run_id"],
            "total_params": rec["total_params"],
            "dense_bytes": rec["dense_bytes"],
            "code_hash": rec["code_hash"],
            "versions": rec["versions"],
            "timestamp": rec["timestamp"],
        },
    }, _checkpoint_path(architecture, seed))

"""Evaluation of a saved dense checkpoint (test set only, no weight updates)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import time

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

from .data import fmnist_split_tensors, load_cora
from .models import build_model, count_params, dense_bytes
from .util import (
    CHECKPOINTS_DIR,
    base_record,
    run_wall_timer,
    set_seed,
    set_threads,
    write_run_record,
)


def load_checkpoint(architecture: str, seed: int):
    path = CHECKPOINTS_DIR / f"{architecture}_seed{seed}.pt"
    if not path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no checkpoint at {path}; run train first")
    payload = torch.load(path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)
    model = build_model(architecture)
    model.load_state_dict(payload["state_dict"])
    return model, payload["metadata"]


def eval(architecture: str, seed: int = 0) -> dict:
    """Evaluate the saved seed checkpoint on val+test. Never updates weights:
    inference_mode + eval() only. Appends a run record."""
    set_threads()
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    rec = base_record(architecture, command="eval")
    rec["seed"] = seed
    try:
        model, meta = load_checkpoint(architecture, seed)
        rec["total_params"] = count_params(model)
        rec["nonzero_params"] = count_params(model)
        rec["dense_bytes"] = dense_bytes(model)
        rec["best_epoch"] = meta.get("best_epoch")
        rec["val_acc"] = meta.get("val_acc")
        rec["val_loss"] = meta.get("val_loss")

        if architecture == "gcn":
            data = load_cora()
            model.eval()
            with torch.inference_mode():
                out = model(data.x, data.edge_index)
                va = out[data.lm_val]
                te = out[data.lm_test]
                rec["val_loss"] = float(nn.functional.cross_entropy(va, data.y[data.lm_val]).item())
                rec["val_acc"] = float((va.argmax(dim=1) == data.y[data.lm_val]).float().mean().item())
                rec["test_acc"] = float((te.argmax(dim=1) == data.y[data.lm_test]).float().mean().item())
        else:
            tr_x, tr_y, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y, _, _ = fmnist_split_tensors()
            model.eval()
            with torch.inference_mode():
                for x, y, kind in ((va_x, va_y, "val"), (te_x, te_y, "test")):
                    n = len(y)
                    correct = 0
                    loss_sum = 0.0
                    bs = 1024
                    for i in range(0, n, bs):
                        xb, yb = x[i:i + bs], y[i:i + bs]
                        out = model(xb)
                        loss_sum += float(nn.functional.cross_entropy(out, yb, reduction="sum").item())
                        correct += int((out.argmax(dim=1) == yb).sum().item())
                    if kind == "val":
                        rec["val_acc"] = correct / n
                        rec["val_loss"] = loss_sum / n
                    else:
                        rec["test_acc"] = correct / n

        rec = run_wall_timer(rec, t0)
        write_run_record(rec)
        return rec
    except Exception as e:
        rec = run_wall_timer(rec, t0)
        rec["status"] = "failed"
        rec["reason"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        write_run_record(rec)
        raise

"""Frozen latency protocol (Part A.1) + analytical MAC estimates.

Latency: torch.inference_mode(), model in eval(). 20 warm-up and 200 timed
iterations, time.perf_counter_ns. Report median and IQR (q3 - q1).
The fixed benchmark input is the first 256 TEST images (inputs only, saved once
to a small file, results/bench/fmnist_bench_input.pt) — NOT training images.
Batch sizes 1 and 256 for Fashion-MNIST; one full-graph forward for Cora.

Memory: the RSS subprocess does not load the 55k training tensor. It loads the
small fixed bench input and the checkpoint, and reports
rss_before_model_bytes (after imports + input load), peak_rss_bytes and
model_rss_delta_bytes = peak - before.

MAC counting (computed from the ACTUAL model's layer shapes — works for any
Linear / Conv2d / GCNConv sizes; nothing is hard-coded). We trace one forward
pass with hooks, and for every weight-bearing module (Linear, Conv2d, GCNConv)
count the MACs its weight performs per single sample:

- Linear(in, out):   each weight element multiplies one input per token;
  MACs = numel(W) * tokens (tokens = 1 here, i.e. per image / per node).
- Conv2d(cin, cout, k): each weight element is applied at every output-pixel
  position; MACs = numel(W) * H_out * W_out per image.
- GCNConv(in, out):   GCNConv computes X @ W ONCE per node (not per edge) and
  then aggregates over the augmented adjacency A' = A + I (self-loops). Per
  layer:
      projection   = N * in * out       (the dense-X weight product)
      aggregation  = (E + N) * out      (weighted sum over the E+N A' entries)
  where N = node count, E = directed edges (A' adds N self-loops).
  The degree-normalization factors D^{1/2} are elementwise scales and add
  ~2 * out * (E+N) multiplications; these are reported separately under
  `gcn_norm_macs` and are NOT part of est_macs.

Two MAC fields are emitted for every model:
- est_macs          : MACs assuming ALL weights are nonzero (dense convention).
                      For GCN this is the dense-X total above.
- est_macs_nonzero  : the same count but only for weight elements that are
                      actually nonzero in the loaded checkpoint (this is what
                      matters once Part B makes the model physically sparse).
GCN additionally reports:
- est_macs_sparse_input : est_macs with the layer-1 projection counted as
                      nnz(X)*out instead of N*in*out, because Cora's features
                      are ~1.3% dense (sparse-input convention).

For the dense seed-0 baselines every weight is nonzero, so
est_macs == est_macs_nonzero.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

from .data import fmnist_split_tensors, load_cora
from .evaln import load_checkpoint
from .models import count_params, dense_bytes, raw_tensor_bytes
from .util import (
    BENCH_DIR,
    ROOT,
    base_record,
    prior_bench_run_ids,
    run_wall_timer,
    set_threads,
    write_run_record,
)

WARMUP = 20
TIMED = 200
BATCH_SIZES = [1, 256]
FMNIST_BENCH_INPUT = BENCH_DIR / "fmnist_bench_input.pt"
CORAL_BENCH_INPUT = BENCH_DIR / "cora_bench_input.pt"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fixed benchmark inputs (inputs only). Saved once, reused by the main process
# and the RSS subprocess so neither ever loads the 55k training tensor.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _ensure_fmnist_bench_input() -> torch.Tensor:
    """First 256 TEST images, inputs only (no labels). Saved once."""
    if FMNIST_BENCH_INPUT.exists():
        return torch.load(FMNIST_BENCH_INPUT, map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
    _, _, _, _, te_x, _, _, _ = fmnist_split_tensors()
    BENCH_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    torch.save(te_x[:256].contiguous(), FMNIST_BENCH_INPUT)
    return torch.load(FMNIST_BENCH_INPUT, map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)


def _ensure_cora_bench_input() -> dict:
    """Full-graph Cora features + edge_index (inputs only). Saved once."""
    if CORAL_BENCH_INPUT.exists():
        return torch.load(CORAL_BENCH_INPUT, map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)
    data = load_cora()
    BENCH_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    payload = {"x": data.x.contiguous(), "edge_index": data.edge_index.contiguous()}
    torch.save(payload, CORAL_BENCH_INPUT)
    return torch.load(CORAL_BENCH_INPUT, map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)


def load_bench_input(architecture: str):
    """Return the fixed benchmark input: (x, edge_index). edge_index is None for
    fmnist; x is the (256,1,28,28) test-image batch for fmnist and the full
    (N,in) Cora feature matrix for gcn."""
    if architecture == "gcn":
        d = _ensure_cora_bench_input()
        return d["x"], d["edge_index"]
    return _ensure_fmnist_bench_input(), None


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MAC estimation from actual layer shapes (no hard-coded numbers).
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _weight_of(mod):
    """The parameter a module multiplies the input by (GCNConv holds it in a
    nested Linear as `lin.weight`; Linear/Conv2d hold it as `.weight`)."""
    w = getattr(mod, "weight", None)
    if w is None and hasattr(mod, "lin"):
        w = mod.lin.weight
    return w


def _mac_entries(model, x, edge_index=None):
    """Run one forward pass, recording (weight numel, weight nnz, out_ch,
    tokens) for each Linear / Conv2d / GCNConv in forward order."""
    from torch_geometric.nn import GCNConv

    model.eval()
    entries = []
    hooks = []
    for name, mod in model.named_modules():
        if isinstance(mod, (nn.Linear, nn.Conv2d)) or type(mod).__name__ == "GCNConv":
            def _hook(m, inp, out, _mod=mod, _name=name):
                w = _weight_of(_mod)
                if w.dim() == 4:  # Conv2d: out is (B, C, H, W); reuse per output pixel
                    tokens = int(out.shape[-2] * out.shape[-1])
                else:            # Linear / GCNConv: out is (B, C) or (N, C)
                    tokens = int(out.numel()) // int(out.shape[-1])
                entries.append({
                    "name": _name,
                    "type": type(_mod).__name__,
                    "numel": int(w.numel()),
                    "nnz": int(w.count_nonzero()),
                    "out_ch": int(out.shape[-1]),
                    "tokens": tokens,
                })
            hooks.append(mod.register_forward_hook(_hook))
    try:
        with torch.inference_mode():
            if edge_index is not None:
                model(x, edge_index)
            else:
                model(x)
    finally:
        for h in hooks:
            h.remove()
    return entries


def estimate_macs(model, x, edge_index=None, x_nnz: int | None = None) -> dict:
    """Analytical MAC estimate computed from the model's actual layer shapes.

    Returns dict with est_macs, est_macs_nonzero, gcn_norm_macs and
    est_macs_sparse_input (GCN only, else None).
    """
    entries = _mac_entries(model, x, edge_index)

    is_gcn = edge_index is not None
    if is_gcn:
        N = int(x.shape[0])
        E = int(edge_index.shape[1])          # directed edges (no self-loops yet)
        E_plus_N = E + N                      # A' = A + I
        norm_macs = 0
    else:
        N = E_plus_N = None
        norm_macs = 0

    est = 0
    est_nz = 0
    est_sparse = None  # computed on first GCNConv layer, else None (non-GCN)
    for e in entries:
        if e["type"] == "GCNConv":
            proj = e["numel"] * e["tokens"]              # N*in*out (dense-X)
            proj_nz = e["nnz"] * e["tokens"]             # nonzero weights only
            agg = E_plus_N * e["out_ch"]
            if est_sparse is None and x_nnz is not None:
                est_sparse = (x_nnz * e["out_ch"]) + agg
            else:
                est_sparse += proj + agg
            est += proj + agg
            est_nz += proj_nz + agg
            norm_macs += 2 * e["out_ch"] * E_plus_N
        else:  # Linear / Conv2d
            est += e["numel"] * e["tokens"]
            est_nz += e["nnz"] * e["tokens"]
            if est_sparse is not None:
                est_sparse += e["numel"] * e["tokens"]

    return {
        "est_macs": est,
        "est_macs_nonzero": est_nz,
        "est_macs_sparse_input": (est_sparse if is_gcn and est_sparse is not None else None),
        "gcn_norm_macs": norm_macs,
    }


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Timing (frozen protocol) and peak-RSS subprocess.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _time_batch(model, x, batch_size: int) -> dict:
    """Frozen protocol: inference_mode, eval(), 20 warm-up / 200 timed iterations.
    A pre-allocated (batch_size, ...) view of the fixed bench input is used each
    iteration so the timed region is the model forward pass only."""
    model.eval()
    with torch.inference_mode():
        xb = x[:batch_size] if len(x) >= batch_size else x
        for _ in range(WARMUP):
            model(xb)
        ns = []
        for _ in range(TIMED):
            t0 = time.perf_counter_ns()
            model(xb)
            ns.append(time.perf_counter_ns() - t0)
    ns = np.asarray(ns, dtype=np.float64) / 1e6
    q1, q2, q3 = np.percentile(ns, [25, 50, 75])
    return {"median_ms": float(q2), "iqr_ms": float(q3 - q1)}


def _bench_peak_rss(architecture: str, seed: int) -> dict:
    """RSS measured in a fresh subprocess that (1) imports + loads the small
    fixed bench input, (2) records rss_before_model_bytes, (3) loads the
    checkpoint and runs a few forwards, recording peak_rss_bytes. Returns
    (rss_before, peak)."""
    code = f"""
import json, psutil, sys
import torch
from lab3.util import set_threads
from lab3.bench import load_bench_input
from lab3.evaln import load_checkpoint
set_threads()
x, ei = load_bench_input("{architecture}")
proc = psutil.Process()
before = proc.memory_info().rss
m, _ = load_checkpoint("{architecture}", {seed})
m.eval()
peak = before
with torch.inference_mode():
    for _ in range(5):
        if "{architecture}" == "gcn":
            m(x, ei)
        else:
            m(x[:256])
        peak = max(peak, proc.memory_info().rss)
print(json.dumps({{"before": int(before), "peak": int(peak)}}))
"""
    proc = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-c", code],
        capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, cwd=str(ROOT),
        env={**os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": str(ROOT / "code")},
    )
    out = json.loads(proc.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1])
    return out


def bench(architecture: str, seed: int = 0) -> dict:
    set_threads()
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    rec = base_record(architecture, command="bench")
    rec["seed"] = seed
    try:
        model, meta = load_checkpoint(architecture, seed)
        # Linkage: parent run is the training run that produced this checkpoint.
        rec["parent_run_id"] = meta.get("run_id")
        rec["supersedes"] = prior_bench_run_ids(architecture, seed)

        rec["total_params"] = count_params(model)
        rec["nonzero_params"] = count_params(model)
        rec["dense_bytes"] = dense_bytes(model)
        rec["raw_tensor_bytes"] = raw_tensor_bytes(model)
        # compressed_bytes is the Part B 'compact export' field; null for dense.
        rec["compressed_bytes"] = None
        rec["best_epoch"] = meta.get("best_epoch")
        rec["val_acc"] = meta.get("val_acc")

        x, ei = load_bench_input(architecture)
        model.eval()

        if architecture == "gcn":
            with torch.inference_mode():
                for _ in range(WARMUP):
                    model(x, ei)
                ns = []
                for _ in range(TIMED):
                    t_start = time.perf_counter_ns()
                    model(x, ei)
                    ns.append(time.perf_counter_ns() - t_start)
            ns = np.asarray(ns, dtype=np.float64) / 1e6
            q1, q2, q3 = np.percentile(ns, [25, 50, 75])
            rec["latency"] = {
                "full_graph": {
                    "median_ms": float(q2),
                    "iqr_ms": float(q3 - q1),
                    "warmup": WARMUP,
                    "iters": TIMED,
                    "threads": torch.get_num_threads(),
                    "batch_size": "full_graph",
                }
            }
            macs = estimate_macs(model, x, ei, x_nnz=int(x.count_nonzero()))
        else:
            lat = {}
            for bs in BATCH_SIZES:
                lat[f"batch_{bs}"] = _time_batch(model, x, bs)
                lat[f"batch_{bs}"].update({"warmup": WARMUP, "iters": TIMED,
                                           "threads": torch.get_num_threads(),
                                           "batch_size": bs})
            rec["latency"] = lat
            macs = estimate_macs(model, x[:1], None)

        rec["est_macs"] = macs["est_macs"]
        rec["est_macs_nonzero"] = macs["est_macs_nonzero"]
        rec["est_macs_sparse_input"] = macs["est_macs_sparse_input"]
        rec["gcn_norm_macs"] = macs["gcn_norm_macs"]

        rss = _bench_peak_rss(architecture, seed)
        rec["rss_before_model_bytes"] = rss["before"]
        rec["peak_rss_bytes"] = rss["peak"]
        rec["model_rss_delta_bytes"] = rss["peak"] - rss["before"]

        rec = run_wall_timer(rec, t0)
        write_run_record(rec)
        return rec
    except Exception as e:
        rec = run_wall_timer(rec, t0)
        rec["status"] = "failed"
        rec["reason"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        write_run_record(rec)
        raise

# Lab 3 `results/runs.jsonl` record schema

Every command (`train`, `eval`, `bench`) appends exactly one JSON object per
attempted run to `results/runs.jsonl` (append-only: lines are never edited or
deleted; a corrected re-bench adds a new line whose `supersedes` lists the
earlier, now-incorrect run_ids). This file documents the fields.

## Identity / linkage

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | str | Unique id for this record: `<arch>-<method>-<UTC timestamp>-<shortuuid>`. |
| `status` | str | `"ok"` or `"failed"`. |
| `reason` | str/null | Failure reason when `status == "failed"`. |
| `part` | str | `"A"` (dense reference). |
| `architecture` | str | `mlp` / `cnn` / `gcn`. |
| `method` | str | `"dense"` for the Part A baseline. |
| `seed` | int | Random seed. |
| `command` | str | `train` / `eval` / `bench`. |
| `parent_run_id` | str/null | For `bench` (and `eval`), the `run_id` of the **training run** that produced the checkpoint being benchmarked. Carried from the checkpoint metadata `run_id`. |
| `supersedes` | list[str] | For a corrected re-bench: the `run_id`s of the earlier bench records for the same (architecture, seed) that are now known to be incorrect (e.g. A1's wrong MAC/byte figures). The old lines remain in the log untouched. |

## Training / selection

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `train_epochs` | int/null | Epochs actually run (may stop early). |
| `finetune_epochs` | int | 0 in Part A. |
| `best_epoch` | int/null | Epoch of the validation-selected checkpoint. |
| `val_acc`, `val_loss` | float/null | Validation accuracy / loss. |
| `test_acc` | float/null | Test accuracy (evaluated only on the selected checkpoint). |

## Size

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `total_params` | int | `sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())`. |
| `nonzero_params` | int | Number of nonzero weight/param elements. For the dense baseline this equals `total_params`; Part B arms report the physically sparse count. |
| `dense_bytes` | int | **Actual on-disk size** (bytes) of a `torch.save(state_dict)` file — the bare state dict (no metadata) written to a temp file, read with `os.path.getsize`. Includes the PyTorch zip/pickle container overhead, so it is slightly larger than `raw_tensor_bytes`. |
| `raw_tensor_bytes` | int | `sum(t.numel() * t.element_size())` over every state_dict tensor — pure payload bytes, no container overhead. |
| `compressed_bytes` | int/null | Size (bytes) of the `dense_bytes` state_dict file gzipped at level 9. This is the "compact export" figure used by Part B. **Null for the dense Part A baseline** (dense has no compressed export). |

## Compute (MAC estimates)

Computed from the actual model's layer shapes (works for any
Linear/Conv2d/GCNConv sizes), not hard-coded. Per single sample (per image /
per node for fmnist-MLP/CNN; full graph for GCN).

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `est_macs` | int | Total forward MACs assuming **all weights are nonzero** (dense convention). |
| `est_macs_nonzero` | int | Same count but only over weight elements that are **actually nonzero** in the loaded checkpoint. Equals `est_macs` for the dense baseline; smaller once Part B prunes weights. |
| `est_macs_sparse_input` | int/null | GCN only: `est_macs` with the layer-1 projection counted as `nnz(X) * out` instead of `N * in * out`, because Cora's node features are ~1.3% dense (sparse-input convention). Null for MLP/CNN. |
| `gcn_norm_macs` | int/null | GCN only: the degree-normalization (D^{1/2}) elementwise scaling multiplications, `2 * out * (E + N)` per GCNConv layer, reported **separately** and excluded from `est_macs`. Null for MLP/CNN. |

### MAC conventions

- **Linear(in, out):** `in * out` per token (1 per image / per node). Bias excluded.
- **Conv2d(cin, cout, k, padding):** `cin * cout * k^2 * H_out * W_out` per image
  (`H_out`/`W_out` are the actual output feature-map dims after padding). MaxPool/ReLU contribute 0.
- **GCNConv(in, out)** (torch_geometric, self-loops added): the weight is applied **once per
  node** (`X @ W`), not per edge. Per layer:
  - projection = `N * in * out` (dense-X weight product),
  - aggregation = `(E + N) * out` (weighted sum over the E directed edges plus N self-loops).
  - `est_macs` = sum over layers of (projection + aggregation); normalization scales go in `gcn_norm_macs`.
  - `est_macs_sparse_input` = `est_macs` but with the layer-1 projection replaced by `nnz(X) * out`.
  - For Cora: N = 2,708, E = 10,556, in1 = 1,433, out1 = 16, in2 = 16, out2 = 7 →
    `est_macs` ≈ 6.27e7, `est_macs_nonzero` = `est_macs` (dense),
    `est_macs_sparse_input` ≈ 1.0e6.

### Dense seed-0 reference values

- MLP: `est_macs` = 234,752 per image.
- CNN: `est_macs` = 1,697,280 per image (conv2 output is 10×10: 28 → conv1 pad2 → 28 →
  pool → 14 → conv2 5×5 no pad → 10 → pool → 5).

## Memory

Measured in a fresh subprocess that (1) imports torch + loads the **small fixed
benchmark input** (never the 55k training tensor), records `rss_before_model_bytes`,
(2) loads the checkpoint and runs a few forwards, recording the peak.

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `rss_before_model_bytes` | int | RSS after imports + benchmark-input load, **before** loading the model. |
| `peak_rss_bytes` | int | Peak RSS observed while loading the model and running forwards. |
| `model_rss_delta_bytes` | int | `peak_rss_bytes - rss_before_model_bytes` — the memory attributable to the model + activations. |

## Latency

Frozen protocol: `torch.inference_mode()`, `model.eval()`, 20 warm-up + 200 timed
iterations, `time.perf_counter_ns`, median and IQR reported. Inputs are the fixed
**benchmark batch** (first 256 TEST images, inputs only) — not training images.

`latency` is a dict keyed by `batch_1` / `batch_256` (fmnist) or `full_graph` (gcn),
each with: `median_ms`, `iqr_ms`, `warmup`, `iters`, `threads`, `batch_size`.

## Provenance

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `wall_time_s` | float | Wall-clock seconds for the command. |
| `code_hash` | str | SHA-256 over all files under `code/` (git-free). |
| `versions` | dict | python / torch / numpy / platform versions. |
| `timestamp` | str | ISO-8601 UTC creation time. |
| `target_sparsity`, `achieved_sparsity`, `stored_precision`, `compute_precision`, `accumulator_precision` | — | 0.0 / "fp32" for the dense baseline. |

## Fixed benchmark input

`results/bench/fmnist_bench_input.pt` = first 256 TEST Fashion-MNIST images,
inputs only (no labels), saved once. `results/bench/cora_bench_input.pt` = full-graph
Cora features + edge_index. These are the latency/RSS inputs and are independent of
the 55k training tensor.

# Lab 3 Part A — Dense baselines (frozen design, predictions.md A.1)

Apple M4 Pro, CPU only, `torch.set_num_threads(4)`, interop threads 1.
Python 3.12 / PyTorch 2.15.0 / torchvision 0.29.2 / torch_geometric 2.8.1 / NumPy 2.5.4.
Split seed 12345 (55k/5k/10k stratified fmnist; Cora 140/500/1000 public split).
Seed-0 rows are the canonical dense checkpoints for the compression arms.

**A2 corrections (supersede the A1 bench rows, which are retained in `runs.jsonl`
untouched and cross-linked via `supersedes` / `parent_run_id`):** the CNN MAC count
(conv2 output is 10×10, not 12×12), the GCN MAC convention (weight applied once per
node, not per edge), and the byte/RSS accounting. All MACs are now computed from the
actual model layer shapes (no hard-coded numbers). See `results/SCHEMA.md` for the
field definitions.

## Sanity targets (test acc, seed 0): all met

| model | target | seed 0 | seed mean (0-3) |
|---|---|---|---|
| MLP | ≥ 82% | **89.29%** | 89.14% |
| CNN | ≥ 87% | **90.87%** | 91.30% |
| GCN | ≥ 65% | **80.80%** | 81.40% |

## Baseline table (seed-0 canonical checkpoints)

| model | val acc (s0) | test acc (s0) | test acc seeds 1-3 | params | dense bytes (on disk) | raw tensor bytes | est. MACs | latency median (IQR) | model RSS Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MLP | 0.8986 | 0.8929 | 0.8935 / 0.8873 / 0.8918 | 235,146 | 943,589 B (0.90 MB) | 940,584 B | 234,752 (per image) | bs1 0.0128 ms (0.0005); bs256 0.1319 ms (0.0046) | 2.38 MB |
| CNN | 0.9182 | 0.9087 | 0.9150 / 0.9134 / 0.9147 | 117,066 | 471,797 B (0.45 MB) | 468,264 B | 1,697,280 (per image) | bs1 0.0930 ms (0.0053); bs256 7.0787 ms (0.1140) | 53.9 MB |
| GCN | 0.8000 | 0.8080 | 0.8070 / 0.8220 / 0.8200 | 23,063 | 94,741 B (0.09 MB) | 92,252 B | 62,697,392 (full graph, dense-X); 1,395,824 sparse-input | full-graph 1.0529 ms (0.0401) | 57.8 MB |

- `dense_bytes` = actual on-disk size of `torch.save(state_dict)` (no metadata),
  via `os.path.getsize`; `raw_tensor_bytes` = `sum(numel × element_size)`; the
  difference is the PyTorch zip/pickle container overhead. `compressed_bytes`
  (Part B "compact export", gzip-9 of the same file) is **null** for the dense baseline.
- MACs computed from the actual layer shapes. Dense baselines have every weight
  nonzero, so `est_macs == est_macs_nonzero` here.
  - MLP: 784·256 + 256·128 + 128·10 = **234,752** per image.
  - CNN: 1·16·25·28·28 + 16·32·25·10·10 + 800·128 + 128·10 = **1,697,280** per image
    (conv2 output is 10×10: 28 → conv1 pad2 → 28 → pool → 14 → conv2 5×5 no pad → 10 → pool → 5).
  - GCN (Cora, N=2708, E=10556): per layer projection `N·in·out` + aggregation
    `(E+N)·out`; weight applied **once per node, not per edge**.
    `est_macs` = 2708·1433·16 + (E+N)·16 + 2708·16·7 + (E+N)·7 = **62,697,392**;
    `est_macs_sparse_input` (layer-1 projection as nnz(X)·16, Cora features ~1.3% dense)
    = **1,395,824**; degree-normalization scales `gcn_norm_macs` = 2·(16+7)·(E+N) = **610,144**
    (reported separately, not in `est_macs`).
- Latency protocol: `torch.inference_mode()`, `eval()`, 20 warm-up / 200 timed iterations,
  `time.perf_counter_ns`, median + IQR. Fixed benchmark batch = first 256 **TEST** images
  (inputs only, saved once to `results/bench/fmnist_bench_input.pt`), not training images;
  batch 1 and 256 for fmnist, one full-graph forward for Cora.
- Memory (RSS) measured in a fresh subprocess that loads the small fixed benchmark
  input + the checkpoint (never the 55k training tensor). `model_rss_delta_bytes` =
  `peak_rss_bytes − rss_before_model_bytes` (RSS after imports+input load, before model).
  (Peak RSS figures in the A1 table included the training-tensor load and are not comparable.)
- Linkage: each bench record carries `parent_run_id` (the training run whose
  `run_id` is stored in the checkpoint) and `supersedes` (the earlier, now-incorrect
  bench run_ids for that checkpoint). Old `runs.jsonl` lines are unedited/undeleted.

## Training (unchanged)

- Training (frozen): MLP/CNN Adam lr 1e-3, wd 0, bs 128, max 30 epochs, patience 5;
  GCN Adam lr 0.01, wd 5e-4, full-batch, max 300 epochs, patience 50.
  Checkpoint = best val acc (ties: lower val loss, then earlier epoch); test evaluated
  only on the selected checkpoint.
- Seed variance (test acc): MLP 88.73-89.35, CNN 90.87-91.50, GCN 80.70-82.20.

## Training stops

| model | best epoch | epochs run | stop reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| MLP | 16 | 21 | patience (no val acc improvement for 5 epochs) |
| CNN | 20 | 25 | patience |
| GCN | 93 | 143 | patience |

## Notes / anomalies

- predictions.md expected test acc ≈ MLP 88-89%, CNN 90-91%, GCN 80-81%: observed
  seed-0 values 89.29 / 90.87 / 80.80 — all inside or above the predicted ranges.
- A1's GCN `est_macs` (306,212,704) counted the weight per edge; the corrected
  dense-X value is 62,697,392 (weight once per node). A1's CNN `est_macs`
  (2,260,480) used a 12×12 conv2 output; corrected to 1,697,280 (10×10).
- Every field is documented in `results/SCHEMA.md`. `results/runs.jsonl` is
  append-only; the corrected seed-0 bench records supersede the A1 ones.

    is_torch_sparse_tensor,

)

@torch.jit._overload
def gcn_norm(  # noqa: F811
        edge_index, edge_weight, num_nodes, improved, add_self_loops, flow,
        dtype):
    # type: (SparseTensor, OptTensor, Optional[int], bool, bool, str, Optional[int]) -> SparseTensor  # noqa
    pass


def gcn_norm(  # noqa: F811
    edge_index: Adj,
    edge_weight: OptTensor = None,
    num_nodes: Optional[int] = None,
    improved: bool = False,
    add_self_loops: bool = True,
    flow: str = "source_to_target",
    dtype: Optional[torch.dtype] = None,
):
    fill_value = 2. if improved else 1.

    if isinstance(edge_index, SparseTensor):
        assert edge_index.size(0) == edge_index.size(1)

        adj_t = edge_index

        if not adj_t.has_value():
            adj_t = adj_t.fill_value(1., dtype=dtype)
        if add_self_loops:
            adj_t = torch_sparse.fill_diag(adj_t, fill_value)

        deg = torch_sparse.sum(adj_t, dim=1)
        deg_inv_sqrt = deg.pow_(-0.5)
        deg_inv_sqrt.masked_fill_(deg_inv_sqrt == float('inf'), 0.)
        adj_t = torch_sparse.mul(adj_t, deg_inv_sqrt.view(-1, 1))
        adj_t = torch_sparse.mul(adj_t, deg_inv_sqrt.view(1, -1))

        return adj_t

    if is_torch_sparse_tensor(edge_index):
        assert edge_index.size(0) == edge_index.size(1)

        if edge_index.layout == torch.sparse_csc:
            raise NotImplementedError("Sparse CSC matrices are not yet "
                                      "supported in 'gcn_norm'")

        adj_t = edge_index
        if add_self_loops:
            adj_t, _ = add_self_loops_fn(adj_t, None, fill_value, num_nodes)

        edge_index, value = to_edge_index(adj_t)
        col, row = edge_index[0], edge_index[1]

        deg = scatter(value, col, 0, dim_size=num_nodes, reduce='sum')
        deg_inv_sqrt = deg.pow_(-0.5)
        deg_inv_sqrt.masked_fill_(deg_inv_sqrt == float('inf'), 0)
        value = deg_inv_sqrt[row] * value * deg_inv_sqrt[col]

        return set_sparse_value(adj_t, value), None

    assert flow in ['source_to_target', 'target_to_source']
    num_nodes = maybe_num_nodes(edge_index, num_nodes)

    if add_self_loops:
        edge_index, edge_weight = add_remaining_self_loops(
            edge_index, edge_weight, fill_value, num_nodes)
